title: Travel bookings
subtitle: book online, accommodation, a package holiday, a city break
summary: Name different types of holiday and use the words you need to book and rent holiday accommodation online.

lesson.heading: Types of holiday
rows: a holiday where you stay near the sea
a winter holiday in the mountains
an unusual, exciting holiday, possibly with some danger, e.g. rock climbing
a holiday with activities for children as well as adults
a holiday where you sleep on a boat and travel from one place to another
a short holiday where you visit a city
lesson.note: We say go on a cruise.

lesson.heading: Booking online
lesson.text: Many people **book** their holiday **accommodation** (a place where you stay) on the Internet. To **book online** you search for your **destination** (the place where you plan to travel) and the dates you want.

examples.text: Many travellers prefer to **book** their holiday online.

lesson.heading: Where to stay
lesson.text: You can look for hotels or **B&Bs** (bed and breakfast: a small hotel where breakfast is included in the price). It is helpful to read the online **reviews** first. A **package holiday** includes the flight, the hotel room and sometimes meals.

examples.text: This hotel has great **reviews** online. Five stars!
examples.note: a review = a description written by people who have been there

examples.text: Here's a nice **B&B** in the countryside.
It was part of a **package holiday**, so the hotel was included in the price.
A popular option for a **weekend break** is to rent an apartment.
examples.note: a weekend break = a short holiday during a weekend

lesson.heading: Renting a private apartment
lesson.text: When you rent an apartment, you often **pick up** (collect) the keys from a neighbour. Then you may need the wi-fi **password**, and you may have questions about what the **listing** promised.

examples.text: We **picked up** the keys from the neighbours.
We can't find the wi-fi **password**. Could you send it to us?
The **listing** said that there was an **iron** in the kitchen.
It's very cold. Where do we **switch on** the **central heating**?

lesson.heading: Words for a rented apartment
rows: a secret group of letters and numbers for connecting to the wi-fi
the written description of something to buy or rent
a small machine that makes clothes smooth and flat
a system that keeps a building warm

lesson.text: *nearby* is an adjective or adverb (a nearby restaurant / there are cafes nearby), but *nearest* is the superlative: the nearest station.

exercises.prompt: Match the holiday types with their descriptions.

pairs.right: you sleep on a boat and travel from place to place
a winter holiday in the mountains
unusual and exciting, possibly with some danger
there are activities for children as well as adults
a short holiday visiting a city

exercises.prompt: Shall we book somewhere for our weekend ___?
exercises.explanation: A weekend break is a short holiday during a weekend.

exercises.prompt: What about this hotel? It has great ___ online. Five stars!
exercises.explanation: A review is a description of a hotel or restaurant written by people who have been there.

options: a small hotel where breakfast is included in the price
a holiday that includes the flight and the hotel
a written description of a place to rent
a short holiday in a city
exercises.explanation: B&B = bed and breakfast: a small hotel where breakfast is included in the price.

exercises.prompt: *Hans:* Have you found any ___ yet? *Paula:* Yes, I've booked a four-star hotel in the city centre.
exercises.explanation: Accommodation is a place where you stay. It is uncountable: no ~~accommodations~~.

exercises.prompt: It was part of a ___, so the hotel was included in the price.
exercises.explanation: A package holiday includes the flight, the hotel room and sometimes meals.

exercises.prompt: Many travellers prefer to ___ their holiday online, rather than on the phone.
exercises.explanation: You book a holiday online: book = make a reservation.

exercises.prompt: Spain is a popular holiday ___ among British holiday-makers.
exercises.hint: (the place where you plan to travel)
exercises.explanation: A destination is a place where you plan to travel.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.right: secret letters and numbers for the wi-fi
the written description of a place to rent
a machine that makes clothes smooth and flat
a system that keeps a building warm

exercises.prompt: I ___ renting a car, as public transport is not very good here.
exercises.explanation: recommend = say that something is good.

exercises.prompt: The ___ train station is a five minute walk away.
exercises.explanation: We say the nearest station, not the ~~nearer~~ station.

exercises.prompt: The apartment is cold. Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: Where do we switch on the central heating?
exercises.explanation: switch on = make something start working.

exercises.statement: When you arrive, you can pick out the keys from the reception desk.
exercises.explanation: When you arrive, you can pick up the keys from the reception desk. pick up = collect.
